monument_name: Vināyaka Kanike Devala 2 (built between the 13th and 15th cent.)
description_en: Kanike Devala 2 is the smaller of twośikharatemples built between the 13th and 15th centuries in a hamlet 500 meters south-east of Vināyaka. They are built side by side on a terrace and face west. The DANAM Identifier for the other temple, Vināyaka Kanike Devala 1 isACH0020.According to Dilli Raj Sharma, “the local people have named them "Kanike Dewal" [lit. temples built in the size of raw broken rice] indicating their smaller size' (Sharma 2012, p. 228). The sanctum of the Devala 2 is empty and has a very limited inner space, allowing only the deposit of offerings. As indicated by the round hole in the sanctum's pavement, it could have held a smallśivaliṅga. This hole could have been used to insert the now-lostśivaliṅga. A small niche carved in the masonry can be found on the sanctum's southern wall. The ceiling is simply decorated with a single circular motif. We do not see the rosette here that usually adorns this part of the monument. There is noāmalakadisc on top of or around the Devala.Suchśikharastemples were built throughout the Karnali Basin from the 13th to the 15th centuries (Andolfatto 2019). The rarity of inscriptions onśikharatemples (locally known asdevala) complicates dating of these type of monuments. The elevation of these two Kanike Devalas is similar to that of the nearby ones in Vināyaka Pañcadevala (ACH0070,ACH0071,ACH0072,ACH0073andACH0074), which were built in and around 1280 CE. The level of theantarāla(Skt.) projection on both sides of the doors is one architectural difference. The projections in Kanike Devalas are shaped like pilasters, whereas in Vināyaka Pañcadevala they are the continuation of the wall's (skt.jaṇghā) mouldings.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université. Sharma, Dilli Raj. 2012. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies.
